title: Microsoft Releases .NET 11 Preview 6 With Language and Framework Updates
gist: Microsoft's .NET 11 Preview 6 completes extension-member indexers and advances union types in C#, adds default cross-origin request protection and a [ShortCircuit] endpoint attribute to ASP.NET Core, and ships a breaking change by dropping the Microsoft.Maui.Controls.Compatibility package.

insights.claim: In .NET 11 Preview 6, C# extension members gain indexer support, letting developers add this[...] access to an existing type from an extension block, which completes the extension-members feature that .NET 10 introduced covering only methods and properties.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Signals Microsoft is incrementally completing multi-release language features (started in .NET 10) rather than shipping them all at once, useful for teams planning migration timing.
insights.locator: In the C# area, extension members now include indexers

insights.claim: Union types in C# advance beyond their Preview 5 introduction: compiler-support types now ship in the .NET framework itself, so a union declaration compiles without hand-written boilerplate, and System.Text.Json can serialize a union by writing its active case, though both features remain preview-only and require the preview language version.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Union types remain experimental and gated behind a preview language flag, so production teams should not adopt them yet but should track their path toward stabilization.
insights.quote: compiler support types now ship in the framework, so a union declaration compiles without hand-written boilerplate
insights.locator: The compiler support types now ship in the framework

insights.claim: Applications built with WebApplication.CreateBuilder in .NET 11 Preview 6 automatically reject unsafe cross-origin requests using the browser's Sec-Fetch-Site and Origin headers, with the protection enabled by default (no configuration required) across Minimal APIs, MVC, Razor Pages, and Blazor.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: A secure-by-default CSRF/cross-origin posture reduces a common class of web app vulnerabilities out of the box, lowering the security burden for teams upgrading to .NET 11.
insights.locator: ASP.NET Core receives a wide set of additions

insights.claim: Because ASP.NET Core in .NET 11 Preview 6 now blocks unsafe cross-origin requests by default, Blazor Web App projects no longer need to explicitly call app.UseAntiforgery(), simplifying the standard app setup.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Teams should check their Blazor startup code after upgrading, since a previously required call becomes redundant.
insights.quote: Blazor Web App projects no longer need to call app.UseAntiforgery()
insights.locator: with a note that Blazor Web App projects no longer need to call app.UseAntiforgery()

insights.claim: A new [ShortCircuit] attribute in .NET 11 Preview 6 lets an ASP.NET Core endpoint run immediately after routing, skipping the rest of the middleware pipeline, and Generated OpenAPI documents now target version 3.2 by default with union types supported as request bodies and return types across the stack.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Gives developers a lightweight way to bypass middleware overhead for latency-sensitive endpoints like health checks or robots.txt.
insights.locator: a new [ShortCircuit] attribute lets an endpoint run immediately after routing

insights.claim: SignalR in .NET 11 Preview 6 can refresh authentication on an existing connection without dropping it, and clients can now cancel non-streaming hub invocations.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Reduces reconnect churn for long-lived real-time apps with token-based auth and gives clients more control over in-flight RPC calls.
insights.locator: SignalR connections can also refresh authentication without dropping

insights.claim: Blazor's Virtualize component in .NET 11 Preview 6 can open at a chosen item and scroll to any item on demand, and client startup behavior can now be configured from the server in C# instead of in JavaScript.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Reduces the need for JavaScript interop in Blazor apps, reinforcing Microsoft's push toward an all-C# development experience for Blazor.
insights.locator: Blazor's Virtualize component can now open at a chosen item

insights.claim: The Blazor Gateway, the development host for standalone WebAssembly apps, can now forward calls to backend services through a built-in YARP reverse proxy in .NET 11 Preview 6, removing the need for CORS configuration during local development.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Simplifies local dev workflows for Blazor WASM apps talking to separate backend APIs, cutting a common source of dev-time friction.
insights.quote: removing the need for CORS configuration
insights.locator: can now forward calls to backend services through a built-in YARP reverse proxy

insights.claim: In .NET 11 Preview 6, the next-generation CollectionView reaches Windows with a handler built on WinUI's ItemsRepeater, and Shell on Android is re-implemented on standard MAUI handlers instead of legacy renderer classes.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Continued migration off legacy renderers toward standard MAUI handlers should improve consistency and performance for cross-platform mobile/desktop UI.

insights.claim: The Microsoft.Maui.Controls.Compatibility package is no longer built or shipped as of .NET 11 Preview 6, a breaking change for any project that references it directly.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Teams still relying on legacy MAUI compatibility APIs must migrate before upgrading to .NET 11, or their build will break.
insights.quote: Microsoft.Maui.Controls.Compatibility package is no longer built or shipped, a breaking change for projects that reference it directly
insights.locator: Important notice is that Microsoft.Maui.Controls.Compatibility package

insights.claim: HybridWebView interop in .NET MAUI now uses a source generator, making it safe for trimmed and Native AOT applications, while Xcode 26.6 becomes the required stable version for Apple workloads in .NET 11 Preview 6.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Apple-platform MAUI developers need to update their Xcode toolchain to stay compatible, and AOT/trimming support broadens MAUI's viability for smaller, faster app binaries.
insights.locator: HybridWebView interop now uses a source generator

themes.theme: Entity Framework Core and Data Access

insights.claim: Entity Framework Core in .NET 11 Preview 6 adds translation of the FullJoin operator to SQL FULL OUTER JOIN, allows keys and indexes to traverse complex-type properties, and introduces an IsConstrained API for relationships that have no database constraint.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Closes long-standing EF Core query and modeling gaps (full outer joins, complex-type indexing) that previously forced raw SQL workarounds.
insights.locator: Entity Framework Core adds translation of the FullJoin operator

insights.claim: The Azure Cosmos DB provider for Entity Framework Core gains index configuration options in .NET 11 Preview 6, and Microsoft.Data.Sqlite now depends on the SQLite3 Multiple Ciphers bundle, giving applications built-in encryption.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Built-in SQLite encryption removes the need for third-party encryption add-ons in apps using Microsoft.Data.Sqlite, simplifying compliance for local/embedded data storage.
insights.quote: Microsoft.Data.Sqlite now depends on the SQLite3 Multiple Ciphers bundle, giving applications built-in encryption
insights.locator: The Azure Cosmos DB provider gains index configuration options

insights.claim: .NET 11 Preview 6 bundles a range of lower-level runtime work: stream adapters for memory and text, activity tracing rules, cross-lane vector operations, runtime-async performance work, JIT improvements, in-process crash report logging, and faster NativeAOT interface dispatch.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Continued JIT and Native AOT investment signals Microsoft's ongoing priority on runtime performance and startup/dispatch speed, relevant to teams evaluating AOT deployment.
insights.locator: Other changes in this release include stream adapters
